@ronag 
> @benjamingr could we use a Set instead of linked list? At least in the non-weak case?

I could not find any indication in the [spec](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget) that would require it to actually be a linked list, no matter that it is defined as such.

I just had a brief look at it and I believe it would even be possible to use a `WeakMap` and also handle weak handles that way (a map, because we need to check for the capture property in this case as well and that could be tracked inside the value. Each type would have it's own WeapMap).

A LinkedList is very slow, I'm not sure a `Set` would be better, it would probably be fastest to build a bitmask of all the options and hold a deque of listeners since I presume listeners are typically added to the end and removed in order from either the end or start in typical use cases.

A `Set` might also work but it's tricky in JS since it would have to be on the function _AND_ the options somehow, so it would mean rolling our own set

issue_context.title: `signal.add/removeEventListener('abort', fn)` is slow
issue_context.body:
Just did a profile of a service in production and noticed that 25% of cpu time goes to add/remove abort listeners. Using signals for async logic doesn't seem to be a very performat solution.

Is there anything we can do to improve this?
